name: Centaur, Urban
source: The Genius Guide to the Talented Bestiary
book: The Genius Guide to the Talented Bestiary

facets.bk: The Genius Guide to the Talented Bestiary

body:
The creature with a male human’s torso and a horse’s body walks with a confident gait.

Urban Centaur CR 5

XP 1,600
Combat (soldier)
N Large monstrous humanoid
Init +1; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +7

DEFENSE

AC 18, touch 9, flat-footed 17 (+6 armor, +1 natural, +2 shield, -1 size)
hp 52 (5d10+25)
Fort +9, Ref +4, Will +3
Weakness undersized weapons

OFFENSE

Speed 50 ft. (35 ft. in armor)
Melee longsword +9 (1d8+5), 2 hooves +4 (1d6+2)
Ranged mighty composite longbow (+5 Str bonus) +6 (1d8+5/x3)
Size 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks bardic performance, sneak attack +3d6

STATISTICS

Str 20, Dex 10, Con 20, Int 11, Wis 8, Cha 15
Base Atk +5; CMB +11; CMD 21 (25 vs. trip)
Feats Cleave, Cosmopolitan B, Power Attack, Quick Draw
Skills Acrobatics +8, Heal +7, Intimidate +10, Perception +7
Languages Common, Elven, Sylvan
SQ evasion, terrain stride (urban), uncanny dodge

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Bardic Performance

An urban centaur has the bardic performance ability of a 5th-level bard, granting him access to the countersong, fascinate, inspire courage, and inspire competence abilities.

ECOLOGY

Environment any urban
Organization solitary, pair, or gang (3-10)
Treasure standard (breastplate, heavy steel shield, longsword, mighty composite longbow [+5 Str bonus], spear, other treasure)

Not all centaurs are creatures of nature, and some seek the allure of cities and civilization. These urban centaurs love to socialize and live within the heart of a metropolis, picking up many of the talents of their humanoid neighbors. Unfortunately, others of their kind ostracize these free-spirited rogues. They can never again return to their forest home, as relations would meet them with only disdain and death. This knowledge drives many to embrace the vices civilization has to offer, and enter into a slow spiral into unhealthy excess. Urban centaurs have a rowdy reputation for brawling, drinking, and gambling. Many offer their services as warriors or bodyguards, but only to fund expensive habits.
